reasoning: I need to revise the subgoal instruction to replace the greedy per-frame nearest-neighbor tracking with a joint tracking rule over the whole shuffle sequence, since cubes swap positions and the current wording risks ambiguity frame-by-frame rather than resolving the assignment globally.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: After the demonstration's put-down, follow that cube through every remaining demonstration frame: in each frame it is the listed cube nearest its position in the previous frame (cubes swap places during the shuffle and move tens of pixels per frame, and lists are sorted by y, not identity; do not assume it returns to its old spot). Point at the cube in the scene at the start of execution nearest its last demonstration position.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: After the demonstration's put-down, follow that cube through the shuffle to the last demonstration frame, tracking jointly rather than frame by frame. (1) The shuffle frames are the consecutive demonstration frames, after the gripper has parked high and 100% open, in which cube positions change by more than a few px. (2) Any cube that keeps the same position (within a few px) through a stretch of shuffle frames is resting during that stretch and is excluded from the matching there; the moving cubes in a stretch are the ones to be assigned (a different pair of cubes may move in a later stretch while the previously moving cube rests). (3) Assign the moving listed cubes in each shuffle frame one-to-one to the tracked moving cubes (never two tracked cubes to one listed cube), and choose, over the whole run of shuffle frames, the single consistent assignment whose total frame-to-frame displacement, summed over all moving cubes and all frames, is smallest. Do not decide each frame on its own: per-frame distances to the two candidates are often nearly equal (differences of a few px or less), a cube can jump 20-30 px between frames, lists are sorted by y, not identity, and the moving cubes may or may not have swapped places by the end (both outcomes occur), so do not assume the grasped cube returns to its old spot and do not assume it ends elsewhere. (4) The grasped cube's position in the last demonstration frame under that assignment is its last position. Point at the cube in the scene at the start of execution nearest its last demonstration position.

revision.refused: The two tie-breaks proposed by the failed step stay out: continuing the cube's prior direction of motion is not committed because in this minibatch a cube that had barely moved in the prior frame gave a prediction favouring the wrong candidate by a couple of px, and assuming the grasped cube returns to its set-down spot when the shuffled cubes finish near their pre-shuffle spots is not committed because in another episode the two shuffled cubes finished exactly at each other's pre-shuffle spots, so that assumption points at the wrong cube there and contradicts the round-1 correction that the cube is not assumed to return to its old spot. The joint minimum-total-displacement assignment committed above is the same criterion the round-1 annotator prompt already used for conflicts, so it extends rather than undoes earlier edits. No memory change is made: picks_done was written and carried correctly at every step, and the later-step point rule (cube nearest the put-down descent) is left unchanged.
